scenarios.assumptions:
The IDS monitors ip_a-ip1 and ip_a-ip2; the ip1-ip2 link and the hosts are unmonitored. Remote login is detectable, so it is disabled on monitored links. sshd BOF has a stealthy strain and ftp .rhosts and local BOF are stealthy, so they stay enabled.
Source: Sheyner, O., Haines, J., Jha, S., Lippmann, R. and Wing, J. M. (2002). Automated Generation and Analysis of Attack Graphs. Proc. 2002 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, pp. 273-284. Section 3 (paper pp. 4-6 of the PDF): connectivity table R, Fig. 3 'Example Network', the four atomic attacks and the sshd-buffer-overflow specification, Fig. 4 'Attack Graph' with its double-boxed path, and Section 3.3.
Transcription notes: PRINTED: hosts ip_a, ip1, ip2; services (Fig. 3) ip1 = ftp, sshd and ip2 = database, ftp; connectivity table R (p. 4): every host has a physical link to every host; ftp port reachable to ip1 and ip2 from all hosts; sshd port reachable only to ip1 from all hosts; ip_a not reachable on ftp/sshd. Trust is initially empty. The intruder starts with root on ip_a. The goal is root on ip2. Detectability per attack (p. 5): sshd BOF has detectable and stealthy variants, ftp .rhosts is stealthy, remote login is detectable, and local BOF is stealthy. The paths ip_a-ip1 and ip_a-ip2 are monitored, ip1-ip2 is not, and there are no host-based IDS components. The full precondition/effect specification is printed only for sshd BOF. INFERRED: the preconditions and effects of ftp .rhosts, remote login and local BOF (from the prose); 'target trusts source' as the .rhosts effect; that rsh needs no port in the table (the table lists only ftp and sshd), so it is allowed on any linked pair; and that both ip1 and ip2 have the ftp-home and xterm/setuid vulnerabilities (not stated per host). DROPPED (not expressible): plvl(T) < root for sshd BOF, the network effect not-ssh_T, and the global 'detected' flag. Detection is encoded instead by disabling detected variants. The detectable strain of sshd BOF is not modelled because the stealthy strain dominates it. 'user_X' means at least user level, so root-producing actions also set user_X. Self-targeted attacks such as .rhosts 1->1 and 2->2 (which appear in Fig. 4) and sshd from ip1 to itself are omitted because they add nothing in a monotone model. Instantiation: 2 sshd BOF (targets with sshd: ip1 only; sources ip_a and ip2), 4 .rhosts, 4 rsh and 2 local BOF, 12 actions in total. Undetected scenario: the expected 4-step path is the one the paper names in Section 3.3 (overflow sshd on host 1, .rhosts to establish rsh trust between hosts 1 and 2, rsh from 1 to 2, local BOF on 2). I computed that it is the unique minimum here. DISCREPANCY: Fig. 4 labels the double-boxed .rhosts node 'att 1, S 0 -> 2' (source ip_a), while the text describes trust between hosts 1 and 2. With my 'target trusts source' effect, .rhosts ip_a->ip2 would enable only rsh ip_a->ip2, which is detected. I follow the text. Fig. 4 also flags the highlighted rsh 1->2 and local BOF 2->2 nodes as D, although the text calls local BOF stealthy. I read the S/D flag as the attack's strain; detection additionally needs a monitored path, and these runs are on unmonitored paths. Detection-ignored scenario: my own computation (3 steps via .rhosts ip_a->ip2, rsh ip_a->ip2, local BOF ip2; unique minimum). The paper's Fig. 4 includes only undetected attacks, so it does not give this case.

semantics: Conditions are persistent Boolean facts; there are no delete effects or negation.
AND requires all incoming inputs; OR requires at least one. Unlabelled joins use the per-scenario AND/OR choice.
An action is enabled when its inputs hold (or it is an approved entry action); executing it assumes success.
Each action executes at most once; efforts are nonnegative, additive, and shared actions are charged once.
Minimum effort is an exact search over closed active sets; limits yield an incomplete result, never a minimum or unreachability.
importDefaults: New imports: root and declared starting conditions true; root actions allowed as entries.
New imports: unlabelled joins default to OR; missing efforts default to 1; goal = reachable node of greatest minimum dependency depth.
